name: Amphiachyris

project_scope.selection_mode: two canonical species, matched morphology comparison

study_strategy.warning: Many Asteraceae look similar from a distance. Use head structure and involucre details, not just a yellow flower photo.

what_they_share: Annual broom-shaped composites with alternate sessile narrow leaves, gland dots and a strong resinous odor when crushed.
Numerous small radiate heads (ray florets and disc florets), with resinous whitish-faced phyllaries.
Functionally staminate disc florets; fertile ray florets form ribbed cypselae with a crown-like pappus.
shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: At a flowering branch, photograph the overall head arrangement (open loose panicle or crowded flat-topped cluster). Then measure a mid-stem leaf width, and inspect a ripe ray cypsela under magnification: rib count and hair length are the strongest confirmation. For difficult specimens inspect the receptacle after removing florets.

rows: Best first visual split; image whole flowering canopy
Overlap at 0.5–2 mm; measure multiple mid-stem leaves
Overlap at 3 mm; photograph with scale
Strong structural separator on dissected mature head
Strong reproductive split on ripe fruit
Pair with rib count, macro scale
species_comparison_matrix.source: Flora of North America, Amphiachyris genus and both species treatments

look_here_first: First separate loose, open flowering panicles (A. amoena) from crowded corymb-like head clusters (A. dracunculoides). Confirm by receptacle texture or ribbed ripe ray cypselae, not flower color.
species_key: Open paniculiform arrays + very narrow leaves usually under 1 mm + receptacle with hooked swollen-based hairs + ray cypselae 4–6-ribbed and long-setulose → A. amoena.
Crowded corymbiform arrays + leaves commonly wider + receptacle deeply pitted and glabrous + ray cypselae 7–9-ribbed and short-setulose → A. dracunculoides.
If only sterile foliage or immature heads are present, retain Amphiachyris sp. until reproductive confirmation.
overlap_cautions: Leaf width overlaps at 0.5–2 mm, plant heights overlap, and phyllary lengths meet at 3 mm; do not force a call from one measure.
Both species have small yellow radiate heads; color does not separate them.

A. dracunculoides canonical species morphology currently calls heads 'discoid or nearly discoid', but Flora of North America describes Amphiachyris heads as radiate. Treat this as a targeted species-card correction handoff, not a genus character.
Fruit characters refer specifically to ray cypselae; sample mature ray fruits rather than mixed disc florets.
Do not infer target-zone nativity from this morphological lesson; preserve each species' existing range metadata.

realistic_lookalikes.distinction: Compare phyllary nervation and pappus/receptacle structure; Amphiachyris has whitish resinous phyllary faces and fertile ray florets with ribbed cypselae. Use mature heads.
Inspect the small composite head, involucre, ray cypsela and pappus rather than broomy habit alone.
Open versus crowded head arrays; hooked receptacle hairs versus glabrous pitted receptacle; 4–6 versus 7–9 cypsela ribs.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.instruction: Side-by-side open paniculiform A. amoena versus crowded corymbiform A. dracunculoides; label branching arrangement.
Remove florets and show hooked swollen-based hairs in A. amoena versus deep pits/glabrous surface in A. dracunculoides; same magnification.
Count 4–6 vs 7–9 ribs and show long vs short setulae with a 1-mm scale.
Photograph multiple leaves against millimeter ruler and label overlap 0.5–2 mm.
Show phyllary lengths 3–4 vs 2–3 mm, resinous whitish faces, and green border absence.
Label yellow ray and disc florets on real photograph to correct misleading 'discoid' learner text; keep overlay provenance separate.

targeted_handoff.request: Reconcile canonical morphology_keys.heads ('discoid or nearly discoid') with Flora of North America Amphiachyris description of radiate heads and A. dracunculoides treatment. Check ray vs disc florets on exact-species material, then update species card without touching range status.
